text:
anya: Quick sync on RBAC UI options. Proposal: a split-invite view where left column is the roles matrix (compact rows) and right column shows a live permission preview for whichever role is hovered or focused. Goal: avoid extra clicks and keep context when exploring roles on desktop. Figma link: https://figma.redwood/split-invite :link:
rachel: Split view could be great for desktop. Concern: how to handle mobile/form-factor where two columns don't fit? Maybe collapse the preview into a sticky bottom sheet on small screens.
tom: Agree on bottom sheet fallback. Also think about a density toggle in the roles matrix: Compact | Comfortable. Power users can use compact and see more roles. Toggle persisted per user.
rui: Accessibility: preview must be reachable via keyboard. If a role row gets focus, the preview should update and we should set `aria-live=polite` text like "Preview: Viewer role, can read projects, logs". Rows should be `role=row` with `aria-selected` state. For mobile bottom sheet, ensure it traps focus when opened and supports screen reader dismissal.
sarah: Copy for preview header: "Viewer — permissions" and summary line: "Can view projects, logs and audit events; cannot invite or change settings." If we persist density toggle, label should be "Row density: Compact / Comfortable" with a tooltip explaining tradeoffs.
ken: Telemetry needs: `rbac.preview_hover`, `rbac.preview_focus`, `rbac.density_toggle_change`, `invite.split_view_used`. Also capture whether preview caused a role change before sending invite.
anya: SSO behavior discussion: for SSO-enforced orgs, adding a role that implies login change should surface a small inline warning in the preview: "Assigning this role requires SSO-linked account" with a lock icon. For the org SSO enforcement switch we discussed requiring typed confirmation when turning enforcement OFF. But product wants to make enabling enforcement also explicit: show a short checklist modal that lists affected users.
rui: Good point — enabling SSO enforcement can orphan non-SSO accounts. Accessibility for that checklist: each affected account row should be focusable and the modal must include a count and summary at the top, e.g., "5 accounts may lose access unless linked". Also provide a CSV download link labelled `Download affected accounts` (accessible name).
tom: For the typed-confirm copy, propose this exact wording for disabling enforcement: "Disabling SSO enforcement may allow sign-ins without your identity provider. To confirm disabling enforcement for <org-name>, type the org name below." Primary CTA: "Disable enforcement" Secondary: "Cancel". For enabling enforcement, use: "Enabling SSO enforcement will block sign-in for accounts not linked to your IdP. Type the org name to continue." CTA: "Enable enforcement"
sarah: Minor copy tweak: replace the word "may" with "might"? Legal likes "may". I'll run it by legal but keep wording concise. Also ensure CTAs are explicit verbs.
ken: Implementation note: when enforcement is toggled we should emit `org.sso.enforcement_changed` with payload including `from`, `to`, and `initiator_id`. Also mark any confirm modal `confirmed_by` in audit.
anya: Audit log UX: when a user comes from the invite flow to Audit > Entries we should keep a contextual filter and surface a small banner: "Filtered by: role=Viewer (from invite)" with a link back. Breadcrumbs should reflect the path: "Invites → Audit Logs" and deep link should include `?from=invite&role=viewer`. Let deep link be copyable.
rui: Keyboard detail: filter banner must be dismissable with `Esc` when focused, and should be reachable in tab order early. Also ensure assistive text announces filter state changes.
tom: Visual accessibility: color used for preview accent must meet AA contrast against background. If using colored tag for SSO-locked roles, use a pattern+color (icon+color) not color alone.
ux-bot: assets: uploaded `rbac/split-invite/v1` + `ssoconfirm/checklist` frames to Figma. :white_check_mark:
anya: Action items:
- Rui: write keyboard + aria spec for split view + modal checklist (due Fri)
- Tom: add density toggle mock + mobile bottom sheet fallback in Figma (due Thu)
- Sarah: finalize copy for both enable/disable SSO workflows and send to legal (due Thu)
- Ken: create telemetry events and audit fields ticket (due Mon)
- Rachel: prototype per-user density preference in prototype (spike)

rachel: ack :thumbsup:

sarah: looping legal now, will update thread

ken: adding events to backlog

anya: Thanks team. We'll run a quick usability test next week focused on discoverability of the preview and the clarity of SSO enforcement modals. :sparkles:
